newsitem.title: JAPAN: Typhoon Rosie heads to sea after killing five.
newsitem.headline: Typhoon Rosie heads to sea after killing five.

text.p: Typhoon Rosie headed out to sea on Sunday after killing five people and injuring more than three dozen in its weekend hammering of southwestern Japan.
The typhoon brought winds of up to 144 kph (90 mph) as it moved into the Sea of Japan away from southwestern regions of Japan's main island Honshu early on Sunday.
The storm, described by Japan's Meteorological Agency as a "medium-sized but powerful" typhoon, was slowly moving northwest over the Sea of Japan, the agency said.
The typhoon affected tens of thousands of travellers at the weekend and caused the cancellation of most sports events on Saturday including Japan's professional J.League soccer all-star match.
In Yamaguchi prefecture in western Japan, two women drowned while picking shellfish in a river, police said.
Earlier on Sunday, three crew members of a car ferry died in a hospital after the 8,015-tonne vessel was hit by high waves.
Police said the typhoon injured at least 39 people.
Air, rail, road and ocean traffic returned to normal on Sunday.
The typhoon forced the cancellation of nearly 500 domestic flights, affecting some 57,000 travellers on Saturday.
As of late Sunday, the typhoon was showing little movement at about 120 km (75 miles) west of Shimane prefecture on the Sea of Japan coast, the agency said.
The typhoon was losing energy and was expected to turn into a tropical storm at around noon (0300 GMT) on Monday, it said.
